answer: Counterparty Sonnet Ledger: each agent must publish a signed sonnet (a short unique verse) binding its ID to a fresh random nonce, and every counterparty it transacts with co-signs and timestamps that verse into a shared ledger. A clone reusing an ID fails nonce-freshness checks, while a new ID needs distinct co-signers who incur velvet-penalty liability if the verse later proves fabricated. Costs: a new nonce plus N co-signatures per clone, and slashed deposits on every forged karst record.
